text:
sasha: quick sync — product asked for more human-friendly audit event names for customer-facing logs. they want names in support UIs and exported CSVs. question: can we adjust naming without breaking SIEMs / RBAC attachments / KMS redaction rules?
eric: short answer: yes, but we need a stable machine-readable id and a separate display_name. keep both.
maria: agreed. propose canonical fields: `event_id` (stable, dot.delimited), `display_name` (human), `schema_version`. RBAC should reference `event_id` only.
tom: product: display_name is critical for support teams and customers. if we can map to event_id reliably, we're good. also want a compact label for mobile UI.
sasha: sample spec I sketched:```
{
  "event_id": "auth.user.login",
  "display_name": "User signed in",
  "category": "authentication",
  "actor_type": "user|service",
  "sensitive_fields": ["ip", "user_email"],
  "redaction_level": "partial|full|none"
}
```
eric: love it. add `immutable_id` comment: the `event_id` must never be renamed — only new ids for semantic changes. renames cause downstream mapping pain.
jess: legal/privacy: ensure display_name never exposes PII. redaction_level must be enforced by ingestion pipeline and KMS encryption policies. we need to record whether fields are encrypted at rest and which KMS key id used.
rory: on KMS: if an event contains BYOK customer secrets we mark `customer_encrypted: true` and attach `kms_key_id`. ingestion should reject messages missing required encryption metadata.
maria: RBAC: rule linkage should be by event_id plus resource patterns (e.g., `auth.user.*`), not display_name. we'll add an `rbac_subjects` array pointing to resource templates.
eric: also planning schema v2 change: add `event_viz_label` for short UI label (max 32 chars) and `compat_aliases` (previous event_ids) so we can do graceful rollouts.
sasha: compatibility question — how do we handle older customer integrations referencing raw event names?
maria: ingestion layer will look for `event_id` or `compat_aliases`. we can emit a migration report listing customers receiving alias mappings.
tom: product asks whether we can make display_name editable by support admins. any concerns?
eric: editable display_name is ok if it's only a presentation layer that maps to event_id. but we must not allow edits that change interpretation. store admin edits separately per-org.
jess: require audit trail for display_name edits (who changed, when). that's meta-audit, but important.
rory: vuln/incident note: if a breach touches audit logs, we must be able to rotate KMS keys and re-encrypt historical entries. design needs key-rotation-friendly metadata: `key_version` and `encryption_algo`.
eric: logging infra: we should keep two copies for customer-facing exports: redacted_public (for customers) and full_internal (for SRE/security with access). both must reference same `event_id`.
audit-bot: deployment: schema-v2 will be rolled behind a feature flag and deployed to staging on Thu 09:00 UTC.
sasha: proposed action items: 1) finalize schema v2 fields by EOD Friday — owners: eric, maria, jess; 2) implement ingestion validation for `kms_key_id`/`customer_encrypted` — owner: rory; 3) RBAC mapping doc for `event_id` patterns — owner: maria; 4) product feature: org-level display_name overrides — owner: tom.
eric: I'll draft schema PR with examples and `compat_aliases` strategy.
maria: I'll draft RBAC crosswalk and integration tests with policies that use glob patterns.
jess: I'll write the privacy checklist for display_name and redaction rules.
sasha: OK — schedule a 30m cross-team sync next Wed 14:00 if that works. @tom @rory please confirm. :calendar:
tom: works for me.
rory: works.
sasha: thanks all. will post the agenda + pre-read in #eng-security. :thumbsup:
